finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so the authorization check is never enforced. Any caller can delete any account. closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete.
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at line 23, which deletes the account

trace.note: Account looked up by attacker-supplied id
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is ignored, so there is no exception and no early return
assertCanDelete is the throwing variant, used only by closeAccount at line 29

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is correct but its result is unused in deleteAccount. No other check, filter or framework annotation exists in the repo (single file). The sibling closeAccount uses assertCanDelete, which confirms the intended behaviour. If the id does not exist, a is null and canDelete throws NullPointerException, which only affects nonexistent ids.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean that is discarded at line 22. assertCanDelete (13-17) throws but is only used by closeAccount at line 29. No other guard, annotation or file exists.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the boolean from canDelete(u, a) is discarded as a bare statement, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated non-owner, non-admin user, unlike closeAccount, which calls the throwing assertCanDelete at line 29.
